findings.title: Git command failure not detected in verify_commit_identity
findings.description: The function doesn't check result.exit_code before accessing stdout. Non-zero exit codes (git not found, repo not initialized) cause the function to return (True, "", "") instead of (False, None, None), which execute_final_gate_agent() treats as a passing check.
findings.recommendation: Check result.exit_code != 0 and return (False, None, None) before calling strip().

findings.title: Command logging path resolution fragility
findings.description: _log_command_to_jsonl walks the directory tree to find .agents/evidence/runs/ and sorts by mtime to pick the latest run. If run directories are created in rapid succession or if mtime is altered, the wrong directory could be selected.
findings.recommendation: Pass the run directory path explicitly through context or environment variable.

findings.title: Silent failure in logging
findings.description: _log_command_to_jsonl catches all exceptions and passes silently. A permission error, disk full, or malformed JSON would never surface.
findings.recommendation: Log failures to stderr or a dedicated error channel so evidence gaps are visible.

findings.title: No credential filtering in command logs
findings.description: Commands are logged as-is to commands.jsonl. If a future change passes credentials through argv (git clone with embedded auth, curl with --user, etc.), they would be written in plaintext.
findings.recommendation: Add a redaction layer that replaces known credential patterns in argv before logging.

findings.title: Modification time race in run directory selection
findings.description: sorted(runs_dir.glob("migration-repair-*"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime, reverse=True) picks the most recently modified directory, not the most recently created. A touch or write to an old run directory would make it "latest."
findings.recommendation: Use the run-id timestamp from the directory name instead of filesystem mtime.
